turns.assessment: The simultaneous bidirectional OSC loss and amplifier input/preamp LOS on both S16–S03 and S16–S07 strongly indicate a physical cable interruption near S16, plausibly one excavation cutting multiple cables in a shared duct. Stable pump currents argue against amplifier failure, while client, line-card, OTN-switch, and WSS faults cannot explain the multi-channel OSC losses. The evidence does not identify one inventory span as the unique repair target, so no single proposal reaches the commitment threshold.

proposals.rationale: O1/O85 and O87/O89 localize bidirectional signal and OSC loss to the S16-adjacent cable section of S16–S03. A common-duct excavation could also account for the simultaneous S16–S07 failure.
O2/O86 and O88/O90 localize bidirectional signal and OSC loss to the S16-adjacent cable section of S16–S07. A common-duct excavation could also account for the simultaneous S16–S03 failure.
Recent work at S16 makes a disconnected line-side patch conceivable, but one OMS input patch would not naturally explain paired OSC losses on two separate line systems.
A disturbed patch at S16 could remove all channels toward S07, but it does not adequately explain the simultaneous bidirectional OSC loss on both S16 links.
